title: Introduce version-gardening sweep and staged retention for embedding + reranker rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a 'version gardening' mechanism and a sweep/retention policy to safely onboard new embedding and reranker model versions, publish performance profiles, and automatically retire stale candidate variants. This reduces catalog bloat, prevents accidental rollouts of untested variants, and ensures profile telemetry maps to actively pinned model versions.
background: We frequently accumulate transient variants during canaries, autoscaling tests, and developer experiments. Those variants clutter the catalog and cause ambiguity in profile-to-deployed mapping. Existing admission gates validate correctness and performance, but we have no automated lifecycle to prune non-adopted artifacts or flag orphaned profiles tied to retired pins.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic sweep job identifies candidate model artifacts not referenced by any active pin or rollout in the last 30 days
Sweep produces reviewable report and moves artifacts into 'quarantine' rather than immediate deletion
Console shows retention status for each artifact (active, quarantined, archived) and links to associated performance profiles
Publishing a profile for a new variant requires a 'pin intent' entry; the profile is only considered 'public' if pin intent exists or variant is actively pinned
Telemetry emits mapping from profile_id -> pinned_variant_id and a countdown for quarantined artifacts
No production rollout is affected (safety: sweep only touches non-pinned, non-production artifacts)
E2E smoke test demonstrating publish -> pin intent -> traffic route in staging passes within CI
proposed_implementation: 1) Add a lightweight metadata field to artifact manifests: last_seen_by_traffic, pin_intent (user/automation who requested pin), retention_state (active|quarantine|archived). 2) Implement periodic 'gardening-sweep' service that: queries catalog, compares against pin/rollout tables and recent traffic logs, and marks candidates for quarantine if inactive for 30d. 3) Quarantine lifecycle: 14d review period exposed in Console with a one-click restore. After review period, move to archived storage tier (cheap blob) with a retained fingerprint for audits. 4) Prevent profile publish from marking a profile as public unless pin_intent exists or a QA gate approves it. 5) Emit telemetry and Cost/Latency deltas for pinned->quarantined transitions so Optimize can advise reclaiming capacity.
rollout_plan: Phase A (staging): implement manifest extension + gardening sweep in read-only mode that only emits reports (2 weeks). Phase B (staging -> canary): enable non-destructive quarantine marking with Console UI and manual restore (1 week). Phase C (controlled): enable archive after review period for non-sensitive artifacts; monitor safety metrics and rollback hooks (2 weeks). Full prod enablement gated on no safety incidents and signoff from SRE and Product.
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit events: gardening.report, artifact.quarantine_started, artifact.quarantine_restored, artifact.archived. Add SLO checks: no more than 0.1% of pinned variants moved to quarantine. Dashboard tracks number of quarantined artifacts, age distribution, and disk/cost savings projection.
qa_and_smoke_tests: 1) CI job that creates temporary artifacts and asserts gardening identifies them after simulated 30d inactivity. 2) E2E scenario where a published profile without pin_intent remains hidden until pin intent is created. 3) Restore flow test via Console API and confirm profile -> pinned mapping reinstated.
implementation_notes: - Make manifest additions backward-compatible: default retention_state=active. - Sweep must run with a dry-run flag before mutation. - Use existing artifact fingerprinting code from ENG-99207 to track provenance. - Quarantine operations must be RBAC-protected and auditable (link audit-log to Private deployments).
open_questions: What exact retention durations should be configurable per project? (default proposal: 30d inactivity -> 14d quarantine -> archive)
Should archived artifacts be restorable automatically via paid support or require manual team assistance?
Do we need a customer-visible opt-out for Private deployments where customers manage their own catalog pruning?
